text.p: Salomon Brothers said in a report released on Sunday that it had raised in its 1997 earnings estimates for Israel's Teledata Communications to $0.95 a share from $0.88.

"We have raised our 1997 projected revenues from $76 million to $81.4 million. For 1998, we expect sales to amount to $104 million, up from the previously expected $98 million," Salomon said, citing the strength of a heavy orders backlog and expectations of major new contracts.
It said it also had upgraded Teledata's 1998 earnings per share (EPS) to $1.25 from $1.15. Salomon set a 12-month price target of $29-$33 a share, compared with a Friday Nasdaq closing of $18 7/8.
Teledata develops, manufactures and sells line concentrators, multiplexers and other products designed to increase the number of subscribers that can be served over public telephone networks.
Salomon said that since the beginning of the year, Teledata had received more than $22 million in new orders that will be supplied by the end of 1997.
"Teledata acquired four new major customers in the fourth quarter of 1996, one in each of the following regions: Africa, Asia, Europe and the Pacific," the report said.
It said Teledata expects to gain three to five new customers in 1997, in South America, Europe and the Far East.
"We believe that Teledata also will be successful in signing important customers in the United States," the report said.
